title: Adaptive batching recommender: profile-driven heuristics and safe rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an adaptive batching recommendation engine that profiles per-workload traffic and emits safe, staged configuration changes for continuous batching and KV/prefix caching. The recommender should produce human-readable suggestions and machine-actionable patches that can be applied via the operator or an automated rollout with rollback triggers. Goal: reduce per-token cost by 8-20% on eligible workloads without violating latency SLOs (p95 latency increase <= 5%). The system must be conservative by default, support canary/staged applies, and maintain audit trails for every recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles computed for >95% of active runtime routes producing sequence_length, inter-arrival, and KV reuse histograms
Recommender outputs: recommended batching window, min_batch_size, max_batch_wait_ms, and cache prefix TTL with rationale text
Automated simulation (replay) estimates cost delta and latency impact; estimated p95 change must be provided for each recommendation
Safe-apply flow implemented: dry-run -> canary (1% traffic) -> staged rollout -> automatic rollback on thresholds
Operator UI shows recommendation diff, risk summary, and one-click apply/rollback in Console
Audit log entry for each apply/rollback including metrics snapshot and operator who approved
E2E tests validating rollback triggers and no data corruption for KV cache changes
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Offline profiler - ingest production traces and build per-route feature vectors (seq len percentiles, arrival lambda, median KV hits)
Phase 2: Heuristics engine - map profiles to candidate configs using simple rules + cost model
Phase 3: Replay simulator - run sampled requests against runtime model to estimate latency/cost impact
Phase 4: Safe apply API - implement dry-run/canary/staged apply with operator overrides and audit logs
Phase 5: Console integration - recommendations list, diff view, and rollout controls
Phase 6: Monitoring/alerts - SLO checks, rollout watchers, and automated rollback executor
Phase 7: Gradual rollout and tuning - collect feedback, tune heuristics and thresholds
heuristics: If median sequence_length < 64 and p95 < 256 -> increase max_batch_wait_ms to capture more concurrent requests
If inter-arrival lambda indicates bursts (coefficient of variation > 1.5) -> favor lower max_batch_wait_ms but higher max_batch_size
When KV reuse ratio > 70% for repeated prefixes -> recommend enabling prefix-level persistent KV cache with TTL aligned to reuse half-life
Avoid increasing batch window for routes with p95_latency_headroom < 10ms; mark as 'no-change'
Prefer batching when GPU utilization < 75% and tokens/sec per-device is below historical optimal throughput
Bias recommendations toward configurations that reduce token cost per-second while keeping simulated p95 increase <= 5%
profiling_signals: concurrency depth and observed batch sizes
KV cache hit/miss ratios by prefix
historical p50/p95 latency and tail error rates
tokens per request and per-second throughput
continuous_batching_config: min_batch_size: recommended minimum number of requests to form a batch (default 2)
max_batch_size: upper limit to avoid latency spikes (default 64, tunable)
max_batch_wait_ms: adaptive wait window; initial recommendation computed from arrival lambda
adaptive_window_factor: multiplies observed inter-arrival to form dynamic wait window
decay_factor: reduces batching aggressiveness on latency regressions
backlog_threshold: do not increase wait window if request backlog > X to avoid queueing
kv_cache_ttl_seconds: suggested TTL per prefix based on reuse half-life
safety_and_rollback: Dry-run mode: recommendations can be simulated without changing live config
Canary rollout: apply to configurable sample (default 1% traffic) for N minutes and collect metrics
Rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 5%, error rate increase > 0.5pp, or cost saving below threshold
Automatic rollback executor that reverts config and notifies on-call Slack channel and create incident ticket template
Manual override: operator can pause rollouts and mark recommendations as 'defer' or 'force-apply' with justification
Immutable audit entry: every apply/rollback must store snapshot of route metrics and recommendation rationale
test_plan: Unit tests for heuristics mapping and cost model calculations
Integration tests with replay simulator using sanitized production traces
Canary e2e tests: apply to staging-like tenant and assert rollback on injected latency
Chaos test: simulate node slowdowns and ensure recommender does not make harmful changes
Load test: validate throughput and GPU utilization improvements on batch-friendly workloads
Security/permissions test: ensure only authorized principals can apply recommendations
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: per-route recommendation history, applied config timeline, estimated vs actual savings
Alert on unexpected post-apply regressions (p95 delta, error-rate delta)
Heartbeat for recommender pipeline: profiling freshness and replay queue length
Audit log monitoring: detect unapproved automated applies
SLO guardrails enforced in Console before allowing rollout beyond canary
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive batching increases tail latency. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and rollback triggers
Risk: stale profiles cause wrong recommendations. Mitigation: profile TTL and continuous re-profiling every 24h or after config change
Risk: cross-tenant interference on Dedicated pools. Mitigation: per-tenant recommendations with capacity-awareness and opt-out flag for Dedicated customers
Risk: incorrect KV cache TTL leading to stale results. Mitigation: require small canary scope for cache changes and monitor cache hit/miss and correctness checks
Risk: operator confusion. Mitigation: rich rationale text, expected impact numbers, and clear Console UX
